title: CFA Level I: Formulas and Definitions
description: For CFA Level I learners reviewing core finance formulas and definitions, including valuation, statistics, accounting ratios, and risk. Original study aid; notation, timing, and model assumptions are stated on each card.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Future value of a single sum with discrete compounding?
cards.back: FV = PV(1 + r)^n. PV is the present sum, r the effective rate per period, and n the number of periods; assume a constant rate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Present value of a single future sum?
cards.back: PV = FV/(1 + r)^n. FV is the amount due after n periods and r is the effective discount rate per period.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Simple-interest future value?
cards.back: FV = PV(1 + rt). r is the simple annual interest rate and t is time in years; interest is not reinvested.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Effective annual rate from a nominal annual rate?
cards.back: EAR = (1 + j/m)^m - 1. j is the nominal annual rate and m is the number of compounding periods per year.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Continuously compounded future value?
cards.back: FV = PV e^(rt). r is the continuously compounded annual rate and t is time in years.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Continuous rate equivalent to an effective annual rate?
cards.back: r_c = ln(1 + EAR), where EAR is the effective annual rate expressed as a decimal.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Present value of an ordinary annuity?
cards.back: PV = PMT[1 - (1 + r)^(-n)]/r. Equal payments PMT occur at the end of n periods; r is the nonzero periodic discount rate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Future value of an ordinary annuity?
cards.back: FV = PMT[(1 + r)^n - 1]/r. Equal payments occur at period ends and r is the nonzero periodic rate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Present value of an annuity due?
cards.back: PV_due = PV_ordinary(1 + r), for the same payment amount, number of payments, and periodic discount rate; due payments occur at period beginnings.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Present value of a level perpetuity?
cards.back: PV = C/r. C is the periodic payment, first paid one period from now, and r is a positive periodic discount rate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Present value of a growing perpetuity?
cards.back: PV = C1/(r - g), with the first cash flow C1 one period from now, constant growth g, and r greater than g.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Present value of a finite growing annuity?
cards.back: PV = C1[1 - ((1 + g)/(1 + r))^n]/(r - g), for n end-of-period payments, first payment C1, and r not equal to g.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Level payment on a fully amortizing loan?
cards.back: PMT = PV r/[1 - (1 + r)^(-n)]. PV is the loan principal, r the nonzero periodic interest rate, and n the number of end-of-period payments.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Net present value?
cards.back: NPV = sum of CF_t/(1 + r)^t over t = 0 through n. CF_0 generally includes the initial outlay and r is the appropriate periodic discount rate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Internal rate of return?
cards.back: IRR is a discount rate that makes NPV equal to zero. Nonconventional cash flows can produce multiple IRRs or no economically useful IRR.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Profitability index for a single initial outlay?
cards.back: PI = PV of future net cash flows / initial investment magnitude. PI above 1 corresponds to positive NPV under these assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Payback period?
cards.back: The time required for cumulative undiscounted net cash inflows to recover the initial investment. It ignores time value and cash flows after recovery.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Discounted payback period?
cards.back: The time required for cumulative discounted net cash inflows to recover the initial investment; it still ignores subsequent cash flows.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Holding-period return?
cards.back: HPR = (P1 - P0 + D)/P0. P0 is the purchase price, P1 the ending price, and D income received during the period, with no intervening external flows.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Arithmetic mean return?
cards.back: Mean = (sum of periodic returns)/n. It summarizes the average single-period return without capturing compounding across periods.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Geometric mean return?
cards.back: G = [product of (1 + R_t)]^(1/n) - 1. It is the constant periodic compounded rate matching the cumulative return, assuming valid nonnegative wealth factors.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Cumulative multi-period return?
cards.back: Cumulative return = product of (1 + R_t) - 1, assuming income is reinvested consistently with the periodic returns.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Time-weighted return?
cards.back: Link subperiod returns geometrically across external cash-flow boundaries: TWR = product of (1 + R_j) - 1. It removes the impact of external cash-flow timing.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Money-weighted return?
cards.back: The internal rate of return on the investor's dated cash flows, including the ending portfolio value; it depends on cash-flow size and timing.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Exact real return?
cards.back: R_real = (1 + R_nominal)/(1 + inflation) - 1, using matching periods.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Approximate real return?
cards.back: R_real is approximately R_nominal - inflation when both rates are sufficiently small; the exact relationship is multiplicative.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for After-tax return on fully taxable interest?
cards.back: R_after = R_before(1 - T), where T is the applicable tax rate; assumes the entire period's interest is taxed at that rate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Coefficient of variation?
cards.back: CV = standard deviation / mean. It expresses dispersion per unit of mean and is most interpretable for a positive nonzero mean.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Population variance?
cards.back: Variance = sum of (x_i - population mean)^2 / N, for all N population observations.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Sample variance?
cards.back: s^2 = sum of (x_i - sample mean)^2 / (n - 1), for n greater than 1; the denominator corrects bias under standard random-sampling assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Standard deviation?
cards.back: The nonnegative square root of variance; it measures dispersion in the same units as the original observations.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Sample covariance?
cards.back: Cov(X,Y) = sum of [(x_i - x_mean)(y_i - y_mean)]/(n - 1), using paired observations.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Correlation coefficient?
cards.back: rho_XY = Cov(X,Y)/(sigma_X sigma_Y), for nonzero standard deviations; it lies between -1 and 1 and describes linear association.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Two-asset portfolio expected return?
cards.back: E(R_p) = w1 E(R1) + w2 E(R2), where the portfolio weights sum to 1.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Two-asset portfolio variance?
cards.back: sigma_p^2 = w1^2 sigma1^2 + w2^2 sigma2^2 + 2w1w2 rho12 sigma1 sigma2. The weights, standard deviations, and correlation must refer to the same period.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Expected value of a discrete variable?
cards.back: E(X) = sum of p_i x_i, where outcomes x_i have probabilities p_i summing to 1.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Variance from a probability distribution?
cards.back: Var(X) = sum of p_i[x_i - E(X)]^2, for discrete outcomes and their probabilities.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Conditional probability?
cards.back: P(A given B) = P(A and B)/P(B), with P(B) greater than zero.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Multiplication rule for probability?
cards.back: P(A and B) = P(A given B)P(B). If A and B are independent, this becomes P(A)P(B).

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Addition rule for probability?
cards.back: P(A or B) = P(A) + P(B) - P(A and B). The intersection is subtracted to avoid double counting.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Bayes' rule for two events?
cards.back: P(A given B) = P(B given A)P(A)/P(B), for P(B) greater than zero.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Expected value of a binomial count?
cards.back: E(X) = np, for n independent trials with common success probability p.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Variance of a binomial count?
cards.back: Var(X) = np(1 - p), for n independent Bernoulli trials with common success probability p.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Standardizing a normally distributed observation?
cards.back: z = (x - mu)/sigma, where mu is the population mean and sigma is the positive population standard deviation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Standard error of the sample mean?
cards.back: SE = sigma/sqrt(n), for independent identically distributed observations with population standard deviation sigma; s/sqrt(n) is the usual estimate when sigma is unknown.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Confidence interval for a mean with known population variance?
cards.back: x_mean ± z_critical sigma/sqrt(n), under a normal population or an appropriate large-sample approximation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for One-sample t statistic for a mean?
cards.back: t = (x_mean - mu0)/(s/sqrt(n)), using n - 1 degrees of freedom under the usual independent normal-sample assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Null hypothesis?
cards.back: The baseline claim tested statistically, typically an equality or no-effect statement; rejecting it requires evidence judged against a significance threshold.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Type I error?
cards.back: Rejecting a true null hypothesis. The chosen significance level alpha controls its probability under the test's assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Type II error?
cards.back: Failing to reject a false null hypothesis. Its probability is beta for a specified alternative.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Statistical power?
cards.back: Power = 1 - beta, the probability of rejecting a false null hypothesis for a specified alternative and testing setup.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for p-value?
cards.back: The probability, assuming the null hypothesis and model are true, of a test statistic at least as extreme as the observed statistic; it is not the probability that the null is true.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Simple linear regression equation?
cards.back: Y_i = b0 + b1 X_i + error_i. b0 is the intercept and b1 the slope relating X to the conditional mean of Y in the model.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for OLS slope in simple linear regression?
cards.back: b1 = sum[(x_i - x_mean)(y_i - y_mean)] / sum[(x_i - x_mean)^2], assuming the denominator is nonzero.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for OLS intercept in simple linear regression?
cards.back: b0 = y_mean - b1 x_mean, where b1 is the estimated slope.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Coefficient of determination?
cards.back: R^2 = 1 - SSE/SST in standard OLS with an intercept. SSE is residual sum of squares and SST is total sum of squares.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Price elasticity of demand?
cards.back: Elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded / percentage change in price. It is usually negative; demand is elastic when its absolute value exceeds 1.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Income elasticity of demand?
cards.back: Income elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded / percentage change in consumer income; positive values indicate normal goods and negative values inferior goods.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Cross-price elasticity of demand?
cards.back: Cross elasticity = percentage change in quantity demanded of A / percentage change in price of B. Positive suggests substitutes; negative suggests complements.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Total revenue?
cards.back: TR = price times quantity sold, when all units sell at the same price.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Marginal revenue?
cards.back: MR = change in total revenue / change in quantity; in a differentiable model it is dTR/dQ.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Marginal cost?
cards.back: MC = change in total cost / change in output; in a differentiable model it is dTC/dQ.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Average total cost?
cards.back: ATC = total cost / quantity = average fixed cost + average variable cost, for positive output.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Economic profit?
cards.back: Economic profit = total revenue - explicit costs - implicit opportunity costs.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Accounting profit?
cards.back: Accounting profit = revenue - recognized accounting expenses; unlike economic profit it does not deduct every implicit opportunity cost.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Profit-maximizing output condition?
cards.back: For an interior optimum, choose output where MR = MC and the crossing supports a maximum; production must also satisfy the relevant shutdown conditions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for GDP expenditure identity?
cards.back: GDP = C + I + G + (X - M): consumption, gross investment, government purchases, exports minus imports. Transfer payments are not government purchases.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for GDP deflator?
cards.back: GDP deflator = nominal GDP / real GDP times 100, using a consistent base-period framework.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Inflation from a price index?
cards.back: Inflation rate = (Index_t - Index_(t-1))/Index_(t-1), usually multiplied by 100 to express a percentage.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Unemployment rate?
cards.back: Unemployment rate = unemployed / labor force times 100. The labor force includes employed and unemployed people as defined by the statistical authority.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Labor-force participation rate?
cards.back: Participation rate = labor force / relevant working-age population times 100.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Fisher relationship between nominal and real rates?
cards.back: 1 + nominal rate = (1 + real rate)(1 + expected inflation); the common approximation is nominal rate = real rate + expected inflation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Current ratio?
cards.back: Current ratio = current assets / current liabilities, using amounts measured at the same reporting date.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Quick ratio?
cards.back: Quick ratio = (cash + short-term marketable investments + receivables)/current liabilities. Inventory and less-liquid prepayments are excluded.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Cash ratio?
cards.back: Cash ratio = (cash + short-term marketable investments)/current liabilities.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Working capital?
cards.back: Working capital = current assets - current liabilities. Operating working capital may use a narrower definition.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Inventory turnover?
cards.back: Inventory turnover = cost of goods sold / average inventory, using a consistent period and measurement basis.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Days of inventory on hand?
cards.back: Days of inventory = days in period / inventory turnover, commonly 365 divided by annual inventory turnover.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Receivables turnover?
cards.back: Receivables turnover = net credit sales / average receivables. Total revenue is sometimes used when credit sales are unavailable.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Days sales outstanding?
cards.back: DSO = days in period / receivables turnover; it estimates the average collection period under the ratio's assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Payables turnover?
cards.back: Payables turnover = purchases / average trade payables; COGS may be used as a proxy only when appropriate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Days payable outstanding?
cards.back: DPO = days in period / payables turnover.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Cash conversion cycle?
cards.back: CCC = days of inventory + days sales outstanding - days payable outstanding.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Total asset turnover?
cards.back: Total asset turnover = revenue / average total assets.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Gross profit margin?
cards.back: Gross margin = (revenue - cost of goods sold)/revenue.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Operating profit margin?
cards.back: Operating margin = operating profit / revenue; the precise operating-profit definition should be used consistently.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Net profit margin?
cards.back: Net margin = net income / revenue.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Return on assets using net income?
cards.back: ROA = net income / average total assets. Other ROA conventions adjust the numerator, so state the convention.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Return on common equity?
cards.back: ROE = net income available to common shareholders / average common shareholders' equity.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Three-part DuPont identity?
cards.back: ROE = net profit margin times total asset turnover times equity multiplier, using consistent net income and average-balance definitions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Equity multiplier?
cards.back: Equity multiplier = average total assets / average equity; it is a financial leverage measure.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Debt-to-equity ratio?
cards.back: Debt-to-equity = interest-bearing debt / shareholders' equity under the stated convention; some analyses use total liabilities, so identify the definition.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Debt-to-assets ratio?
cards.back: Debt-to-assets = interest-bearing debt / total assets under the stated convention; total liabilities to assets is a related but different ratio.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Interest coverage ratio?
cards.back: Interest coverage = EBIT / interest expense, using earnings before interest and taxes.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Basic earnings per share?
cards.back: Basic EPS = (net income - preferred dividends)/weighted-average common shares outstanding, with adjustments as required for the applicable reporting framework.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Price-to-earnings ratio?
cards.back: P/E = share price / earnings per share. Identify whether EPS is trailing or forward and whether earnings are normalized.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Price-to-book ratio?
cards.back: P/B = market price per common share / book value per common share; positive book equity is needed for ordinary interpretation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Dividend yield?
cards.back: Dividend yield = annual dividends per share / share price. State whether dividends are trailing or expected.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Dividend payout ratio?
cards.back: Payout ratio = common dividends / net income available to common shareholders, equivalently dividends per share / corresponding EPS.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Retention ratio?
cards.back: Retention ratio = 1 - dividend payout ratio; it is the fraction of earnings retained under consistent definitions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Sustainable growth rate under a stable financing policy?
cards.back: g = retention ratio times ROE, in the common constant-ROE model with no new common equity and a stable capital structure and payout policy.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Accounting equation?
cards.back: Assets = liabilities + equity. It expresses the balance-sheet relationship at a point in time.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Ending retained earnings?
cards.back: Ending retained earnings = beginning retained earnings + net income - dividends, absent other direct adjustments.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Straight-line depreciation?
cards.back: Annual depreciation = (asset cost - estimated residual value)/estimated useful life, for a full year under straight-line allocation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Double-declining-balance depreciation?
cards.back: Annual depreciation = (2/useful life) times beginning depreciable book value, subject to the residual-value floor and appropriate partial-year rules.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Inventory cost flow under FIFO?
cards.back: First-in, first-out assigns the earliest inventory costs to cost of goods sold and leaves more recent costs in ending inventory.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Inventory cost flow under LIFO?
cards.back: Last-in, first-out assigns the latest inventory costs to cost of goods sold and leaves older layers in inventory. Availability depends on the reporting framework.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Weighted-average inventory unit cost?
cards.back: Average unit cost = total cost of goods available / total units available, under a periodic weighted-average system.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Cost of goods sold from inventory balances?
cards.back: COGS = beginning inventory + purchases and other inventoriable additions - ending inventory, with consistent treatment of returns and adjustments.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Change in LIFO reserve and COGS?
cards.back: FIFO COGS = LIFO COGS - change in LIFO reserve, where the reserve is FIFO inventory minus LIFO inventory and other adjustments are absent.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Book value of a depreciable asset?
cards.back: Carrying amount = historical cost - accumulated depreciation - accumulated impairment, under a historical-cost model without revaluation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Indirect operating cash flow starting from net income?
cards.back: CFO = net income + noncash expenses - noncash gains, adjusted for operating working-capital changes and applicable cash-flow classification rules.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Effect of an increase in operating receivables on indirect CFO?
cards.back: Subtract the increase from net income, all else equal, because recognized revenue exceeded associated cash collections.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Effect of an increase in operating payables on indirect CFO?
cards.back: Add the increase to net income, all else equal, because recognized expenses or purchases exceeded related cash payments.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Free cash flow to the firm from EBIT?
cards.back: FCFF = EBIT(1 - T) + depreciation and amortization - capital expenditures - increase in operating working capital, in a simplified model with consistent tax assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Free cash flow to equity from net income?
cards.back: FCFE = net income + depreciation and amortization - capital expenditures - increase in operating working capital + net borrowing, in a simplified model.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for NOPAT?
cards.back: Net operating profit after tax = EBIT(1 - T), using an appropriate operating tax rate T under the simplified model.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Economic profit using invested capital?
cards.back: Economic profit = NOPAT - WACC times invested capital. Use consistent timing, usually beginning invested capital for a period's charge.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Weighted-average cost of capital?
cards.back: WACC = w_d r_d(1 - T) + w_p r_p + w_e r_e. Weights use the chosen target market-value capital structure and sum to 1; the tax shield must be applicable.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Cost of perpetual preferred equity?
cards.back: r_p = preferred dividend per period / net issue price or current market price, with consistent valuation purpose and level perpetual dividends.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for CAPM required return on equity?
cards.back: E(R_i) = R_f + beta_i[E(R_m) - R_f]. R_f is the risk-free rate and E(R_m) - R_f the expected market risk premium.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Beta from covariance?
cards.back: beta_i = Cov(R_i,R_m)/Var(R_m), for a market return with positive variance.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Portfolio beta?
cards.back: beta_p = sum of w_i beta_i, using consistent benchmark betas and portfolio weights.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Market risk premium?
cards.back: Market risk premium = expected market return - risk-free rate, for matching horizons and currency.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Security market line?
cards.back: The CAPM relationship between expected return and beta: E(R_i) = R_f + beta_i times market risk premium.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Capital market line?
cards.back: E(R_p) = R_f + [(E(R_m) - R_f)/sigma_m]sigma_p for efficient combinations of a risk-free asset and the market portfolio under CAPM assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Sharpe ratio?
cards.back: Sharpe ratio = (portfolio return - risk-free return)/portfolio standard deviation, using consistent periods and a stated expected or historical-return convention.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Treynor ratio?
cards.back: Treynor ratio = (portfolio return - risk-free return)/portfolio beta, typically interpreted for well-diversified portfolios with positive beta.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Jensen's alpha?
cards.back: Alpha = R_p - [R_f + beta_p(R_m - R_f)], with consistent realized-return inputs for a historical estimate.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Tracking error?
cards.back: The standard deviation of active returns, where active return = portfolio return - benchmark return over matching periods.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Information ratio?
cards.back: Information ratio = mean active return / tracking error, using matching period conventions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Systematic risk?
cards.back: Risk associated with broad common factors that cannot be eliminated merely by diversifying across securities exposed to those factors.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Unsystematic risk?
cards.back: Issuer-specific or idiosyncratic risk that can be reduced through diversification, subject to portfolio construction and common exposures.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Diversification benefit in a two-asset portfolio?
cards.back: When correlation is below +1, portfolio standard deviation is below the weighted average of component standard deviations for positive weights and nonzero volatilities.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Minimum-variance portfolio?
cards.back: The portfolio with the lowest variance among a specified feasible set of portfolio weights; constraints and the available assets determine the solution.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Efficient frontier?
cards.back: The set of feasible risky portfolios with the greatest expected return for each risk level, or least risk for each expected return.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Utility with mean-variance preferences?
cards.back: U = E(R) - 0.5A sigma^2, where A is risk aversion and returns and variance must use a consistent numeric convention.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Optimal risky weight in a simple mean-variance model?
cards.back: y = [E(R_risky) - R_f]/(A sigma_risky^2), absent borrowing or short-sale constraints and under the model's quadratic utility approximation.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Bond price using a constant yield per coupon period?
cards.back: P = sum of C/(1 + y)^t for t = 1 to n, plus face value/(1 + y)^n. C is coupon per period and y is yield per coupon period; settlement is on a coupon date.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Price of a zero-coupon bond?
cards.back: P = F/(1 + y)^n, where F is face value and y and n use matching compounding periods.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Current yield on a bond?
cards.back: Current yield = annual coupon cash flow / current bond price. It excludes capital gain or loss and reinvestment effects.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Yield to maturity?
cards.back: The discount rate equating a bond's price with promised remaining coupons and principal under a specified compounding convention. Realized return also depends on default, reinvestment, and holding period.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Coupon payment per period?
cards.back: Coupon payment = face value times annual coupon rate / number of coupon payments per year.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Bond clean and dirty prices?
cards.back: Dirty price = clean price + accrued interest. Dirty price is the full settlement price before transaction costs.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Accrued interest on a conventional fixed-rate bond?
cards.back: Accrued interest = coupon per period times fraction of the coupon period elapsed, using the bond's applicable day-count convention.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Bond price-yield relationship?
cards.back: For a conventional option-free fixed-rate bond with positive cash flows, price falls when required yield rises and rises when yield falls, other factors unchanged.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Premium bond condition?
cards.back: On a coupon date for a conventional fixed-rate bond, price exceeds par when its coupon rate exceeds its quoted YTM on a comparable basis.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Discount bond condition?
cards.back: On a coupon date for a conventional fixed-rate bond, price is below par when its coupon rate is below its quoted YTM on a comparable basis.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Par bond condition?
cards.back: On a coupon date for a conventional fixed-rate bond, price equals par when the coupon rate equals the YTM on a comparable basis.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Macaulay duration?
cards.back: D_Mac = sum of t times PV(CF_t) / full price, where t is measured in years and cash flows are discounted consistently with the yield convention.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Modified duration?
cards.back: D_mod = D_Mac/(1 + y/m), where y is nominal annual YTM compounded m times per year and Macaulay duration is in years.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for First-order bond price change using modified duration?
cards.back: Delta P/P is approximately -D_mod Delta y, with Delta y expressed as a decimal annual yield change and conventions consistent with duration.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Dollar duration?
cards.back: Dollar duration = modified duration times full bond price or position value, depending on the stated unit; it measures approximate currency sensitivity to a unit yield change.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Price value of a basis point?
cards.back: PVBP is approximately modified duration times full price times 0.0001. It is the magnitude of the estimated price change for a one-basis-point yield move.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Duration-convexity bond price approximation?
cards.back: Delta P/P is approximately -D_mod Delta y + 0.5 Convexity(Delta y)^2, with all yield and time conventions consistent.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Effective duration?
cards.back: D_eff = (P_down - P_up)/(2 P0 Delta curve), using model prices after small parallel benchmark-curve shifts and allowing option-dependent cash flows to change.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Effective convexity?
cards.back: C_eff = (P_down + P_up - 2P0)/(P0 Delta curve^2), using symmetric benchmark-curve shifts and model-based full prices.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Macaulay duration of a zero-coupon bond?
cards.back: It equals the time to maturity because the only cash flow occurs at maturity.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Credit spread?
cards.back: The yield difference between a credit-risky instrument and a specified benchmark, with comparable maturity and explicit yield conventions; spread can reflect more than default risk.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Expected credit loss in a simple one-period model?
cards.back: Expected loss = probability of default times loss given default times exposure at default, using compatible definitions and the relevant horizon.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Loss given default?
cards.back: LGD = 1 - recovery rate when both are expressed as fractions of the same exposure and measured on a consistent basis.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Spot rate?
cards.back: A discount rate applicable to a single cash flow at a specified maturity; a collection of these rates forms a spot curve.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Bond value using spot rates?
cards.back: P = sum of CF_t/(1 + s_t)^t, with annual effective spot rates s_t and cash flows at year t; use corresponding factors for other conventions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for One-year forward rate beginning one year from now?
cards.back: f_1,2 = (1 + s2)^2/(1 + s1) - 1, where s1 and s2 are annual effective one- and two-year spot rates under no-arbitrage assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for General forward rate from annual effective spot rates?
cards.back: For t2 greater than t1, (1 + f)^(t2 - t1) = (1 + s_t2)^t2/(1 + s_t1)^t1, with f the annual effective forward rate over that interval.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Reinvestment risk?
cards.back: The risk that interim cash flows must be reinvested at rates lower than anticipated, reducing the realized return for a given horizon.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Call risk for a bondholder?
cards.back: The risk that an issuer redeems a callable bond under its terms, often when rates fall, limiting price appreciation and creating reinvestment needs.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Put option embedded in a bond?
cards.back: A contractual right allowing the bondholder to sell the bond back to the issuer under specified terms; it generally benefits the holder relative to an otherwise identical nonputable bond.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Floating-rate coupon?
cards.back: Coupon rate = reference rate fixed under the contract + contractual spread, subject to any cap, floor, and reset conventions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Gordon growth equity value?
cards.back: P0 = D1/(r - g), with next period's dividend D1, constant perpetual growth g, and required equity return r greater than g.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Required return from the Gordon model?
cards.back: r = D1/P0 + g, where D1/P0 is the forward dividend yield and g the sustainable constant growth assumed by the model.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for No-growth dividend-discount value?
cards.back: P0 = D/r for a level dividend D paid every period forever, first paid one period from now, with positive required return r.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Multistage dividend-discount value?
cards.back: P0 = sum of D_t/(1 + r)^t during the explicit forecast plus terminal value/(1 + r)^N, where terminal value is measured at the end of year N.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Terminal value under Gordon growth?
cards.back: TV_N = D_(N+1)/(r - g), with r greater than g and stable growth beginning after the explicit forecast period.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Justified forward P/E in the Gordon model?
cards.back: P0/E1 = payout ratio/(r - g), using next period's earnings E1, constant payout, and r greater than g.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Enterprise value, simplified?
cards.back: EV = market value of common equity + preferred equity + debt + noncontrolling interests - cash and nonoperating cash equivalents, under a stated convention.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for EV-to-EBITDA multiple?
cards.back: EV/EBITDA = enterprise value / earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation, and amortization; ensure consistent operating scope and period.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Price-to-sales ratio?
cards.back: P/S = equity market value / revenue, or price per share divided by revenue per share, with a consistent share-count basis.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Residual income?
cards.back: RI_t = earnings available to common equity_t - required equity return times beginning common book equity, using consistent accounting assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Equity value in a residual-income model?
cards.back: V0 = B0 + sum of RI_t/(1 + r)^t, where B0 is current common book equity and the model requires consistent clean-surplus and terminal-value treatment.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Forward contract?
cards.back: An agreement to buy or sell an underlying asset at a specified future time for an agreed delivery price; terms are commonly customized.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Futures contract?
cards.back: A standardized exchange-traded derivative with contractual future delivery or settlement and typically daily marking to market.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Long forward payoff at maturity?
cards.back: Payoff = S_T - K per unit, where S_T is the underlying spot price at maturity and K is the contracted delivery price; financing and transaction costs are excluded.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Short forward payoff at maturity?
cards.back: Payoff = K - S_T per unit, excluding financing and transaction costs.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Forward price for a non-income-producing asset?
cards.back: F0 = S0(1 + r)^T with annual effective risk-free rate r, time T in years, and frictionless borrowing, lending, and short-selling assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Forward price with known discrete cash income?
cards.back: F0 = (S0 - PV of income)(1 + r)^T, under consistent discounting and no-arbitrage assumptions with known income paid before maturity.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Forward price with continuous dividend yield?
cards.back: F0 = S0 e^((r - q)T), with continuously compounded financing rate r and continuous proportional dividend yield q.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Currency forward quote under covered interest parity?
cards.back: F_domestic/foreign = S_domestic/foreign(1 + r_domestic)^T/(1 + r_foreign)^T, using annual effective rates for matching maturities and ideal no-arbitrage conditions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for European call option payoff?
cards.back: Payoff = max(S_T - K, 0) per unit at expiration; K is strike and S_T is underlying price.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for European put option payoff?
cards.back: Payoff = max(K - S_T, 0) per unit at expiration.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Long call profit at expiration ignoring financing?
cards.back: Profit = max(S_T - K, 0) - premium paid, per unit and excluding fees and the time value of the premium.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Long put profit at expiration ignoring financing?
cards.back: Profit = max(K - S_T, 0) - premium paid, per unit and excluding fees and the time value of the premium.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Call option intrinsic value?
cards.back: Intrinsic value = max(S - K, 0), using current underlying price S and strike K.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Put option intrinsic value?
cards.back: Intrinsic value = max(K - S, 0), using current underlying price S and strike K.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for European put-call parity without dividends?
cards.back: c + PV(K) = p + S0, for European options on the same non-dividend-paying asset with the same strike and maturity under no-arbitrage assumptions.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Long call break-even at expiration ignoring financing?
cards.back: Break-even underlying price = strike + premium paid, excluding fees and the time value of the premium.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Long put break-even at expiration ignoring financing?
cards.back: Break-even underlying price = strike - premium paid, excluding fees and the time value of the premium.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Interest-rate swap, plain vanilla?
cards.back: An agreement to exchange fixed-rate and floating-rate interest cash flows on a stated notional amount under specified payment and reset conventions; principal is usually not exchanged.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Hedge ratio using position values and betas?
cards.back: For a simple equity futures beta hedge, N = (beta_current - beta_target) times portfolio value / futures contract value, assuming futures beta near 1 and an appropriate index match; positive N denotes contracts to sell.

cards.front: What is the formula or definition for Leverage ratio based on assets and investor equity?
cards.back: Leverage = total asset exposure / investor equity. In a simple financed position, borrowing increases both exposure per equity unit and sensitivity of equity returns.
